item.research_question: How does phase separation (specifically Cu-rich grain boundaries and Cu-rich grains) affect the mechanical properties and nanoscale deformation mechanisms of the Co–Cr–Cu–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloy under uniaxial tensile loading?
item.material_system: Co–Cr–Cu–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloy (equiatomic composition with Cu-rich regions up to 80% Cu content)
item.processing_route: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation using LAMMPS code with Farkas et al. interatomic potential; models constructed as 2D sheets (60 × 60 × 3.62 nm³, 1,098,730 atoms) and 3D cubes (23.4 nm side, 1,080,458 atoms); equilibration via energy minimization, 2 ns relaxation at 5 GPa/300 K, and 2 ns relaxation at 0 GPa/300 K; uniaxial tensile deformation applied at 300 K with a strain rate of 4.0 × 10⁷ s⁻¹
item.test_conditions: Uniaxial tensile loading along the X-direction at 300 K; strain rate of 4.0 × 10⁷ s⁻¹; periodic boundary conditions in all three directions; analysis via adaptive common-neighbor analysis (CNA) and atomic strain modifiers
key_findings: Cu-rich grain boundaries significantly reduced ductility, causing intergranular fracture at 7.4% strain in 2D samples and 7.8% strain in 3D samples.
The yield strength of samples with Cu-rich grain boundaries was lower than random composition distribution (RCD) samples.
Cu-rich grains lowered the overall strength of the alloy, with the strength decrease becoming more obvious as the volume fraction of Cu-rich grains increased.
The critical resolved shear stress (CRSS) of Cu-depleted grains was greater than that of Cu-rich grains, meaning slip systems in Cu-rich grains activated first.
Dislocation slipping and grain boundary sliding were identified as the main mechanisms of plastic deformation.
The internal slip system was predominantly of the <112>{111} type rather than the common <110>{111} type due to lattice distortion and energy considerations.
An uneven stress distribution was observed where the stress on Cu-depleted grains was much higher than that on Cu-rich grains.
item.mechanism: Phase separation creates regions with different mechanical properties; Cu-rich regions have lower strength and lower critical resolved shear stress, causing plastic deformation to initiate there first. In Cu-rich grain boundary samples, the low strength of the boundaries leads to early cracking and intergranular fracture, reducing ductility. In Cu-rich grain samples, the lower CRSS of Cu-rich grains causes them to yield first, lowering the macroscopic strength, while the stress concentration in Cu-depleted grains can sometimes override this if the stress distribution is uneven.
item.limitations: The simulations used a relatively high loading rate of 4.0 × 10⁷ s⁻¹ due to timescale limitations of MD, ideal crystal structures, and extreme purity, leading to considerably higher yield stress compared to conventional experiments.
item.future_work: The theoretical investigation of phase separation influence on deformation behaviors may inspire new ideas to improve the mechanical properties of the alloy and expand its practical application.
quotes: Cu-rich grain boundaries significantly reduced ductility.
Dislocation slipping and grain boundary sliding were the main mechanisms of plastic deformation in the Co–Cr–Cu–Fe–Ni HEA.
The CRSS of the Cu-depleted grains was greater than that of the Cu-rich grains.
